claims.statement: The Enterprise Web App credential (admin authentication, available only to Adobe Technology Partner Program partners) lets the partner's backend generate access tokens for a customer organization's technical account using its own client_id, client_secret and the customer org_id.

sources.supports: The partner app can use its client_id and client_secret and the customer org_id to generate access tokens; the credential requires a secure backend server; only available to TPP partners.
sources.locator: sections "Enterprise Web App credential" and "How does it work?"

sources.supports: Admin authentication lists the Enterprise Web App credential.

claims.statement: For the Enterprise Web App credential the client secret is sent to the token endpoint as the form parameter client_secret, together with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, scope and the customer org_id (taken from the org_id claim of a verified id_token); the response carries an access_token and expires_in and no refresh token.

sources.supports: The generate-access-token cURL request posts grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, scope and org_id as form data, with placeholders for each; the sample response has access_token and expires_in.

The org_id is extracted from the id_token org_id claim and used with client_id, client_secret and scopes to generate access tokens; no refresh tokens are generated because the partner app can use client_id, client_secret, scope and org_id at any time.
sources.locator: sections "Step 3: Generating access tokens after the admin consents" and "Refreshing access tokens"

claims.statement: The Enterprise Web App client secret is rotated through the Developer Console UI by adding a new secret, replacing the old one in the application, checking the last-used timestamp and deleting the old one; a deleted secret cannot be restored, and programmatic rotation is not currently supported.

sources.supports: Client secret for the Enterprise Web App credential can be rotated through the Dev Console UI; once deleted a secret cannot be restored; programmatic rotation of Enterprise Web App client secrets is not currently supported.
sources.locator: sections "Rotating client secrets" and "Rotating client secrets programmatically"

claims.statement: The Enterprise Web App pages show the client secret only as the placeholder <YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET> (and the access_token as a truncated ey..... placeholder); no page read states a prefix, alphabet, length or checksum for the secret. The id_token returned in the consent redirect is a signed JSON web token for the partner app to verify and is a separate artifact from the client secret.

sources.supports: cURL request and sample response use <YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET> and "ey....." placeholders; id_token is described as a well formed JSON web token with claims iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, org_id and nonce.
sources.locator: sections "Generate Access Token Request" and "Redirect URL"

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Re-read 2026-10-05: the existing claim is unchanged and three claims about the token-request carrier, rotation and the absence of a documented format are added. The p8e- prefix recorded for another family is deliberately not copied here: no source attributes it to this credential type.

openQuestions.question: Adobe documentation read for this candidate gives no prefix, alphabet, length or other format rule for this value; any example in it is a placeholder or a public identifier. Not researched beyond existence.

The pages read do not show whether this client secret differs in shape or handling from the OAuth Web App or OAuth Server-to-Server client secrets; it is kept as a separate candidate because it belongs to a different credential type, holder (a partner, not the customer) and authentication type. The merge-or-split question is open.

Whether an Adobe client secret beginning p8e- (treated as an Adobe client secret, type unnamed, by two scanner rule artifacts; see the OAuth Server-to-Server contract) can be an Enterprise Web App client secret is not established; the provider pages read do not mention the prefix. Settled by an Adobe statement tying the prefix to a credential type.
The pages read do not state how many client secrets an Enterprise Web App credential can hold or whether a secret is shown once. Settled by an Adobe page on Enterprise Web App credential management.
